name: Copper
description: Copper! The furnace becomes a smelter, and new ores are found.

name: Bronze
description: The Bronze Age, and the brewers and vintners of Sumer and Egypt: the Fermenter is unlocked.

name: Brass
description: Bronze and brass buy gold-bearing gravel and quartz, silver ore, cinnabar and kohl from the traders.

name: Iron
description: The Iron Age. Distillation is invented, and the markets of antiquity open.

name: Glass
description: Glass vessels: you can now chill and crystallise in an ice bath.

name: Ethanol
description: Spirit of wine. The perfumers turn the still on the herb garden.

name: Acetic Acid
description: Vinegar keeps the harvest: the pantry and the apothecary's jars fill up.

name: Sulfuric Acid
description: Oil of vitriol. The alchemists' cabinet fills with strange salts.

name: Nitric Acid
description: Aqua fortis eats metal and stone; only glass can hold it. The Glass Flask is unlocked.

name: White phosphorus
description: Brand's phosphorus ends the age of alchemy. Coal, air and the mineral cabinets of the new chemists.

name: Silver Chloride
description: Horn silver darkens in the sun: light itself can drive chemistry.

name: Coke
description: Abraham Darby's coke (1709) burns hot enough to smelt iron by the ton: the Blast Furnace is unlocked.

name: Pig Iron
description: Coke iron makes boilers: Papin's digester becomes the Autoclave, and the mines go deeper.

name: Vulcanised Rubber
description: Goodyear's rubber: long chains are a material of their own. Polymerisation unlocked.

name: Hydrogen
description: Cavendish's inflammable air. The hunt for new elements begins in earnest.

name: Chlorine
description: Scheele's chlorine bleaches linen, and chemists start taking apart animal and vegetable matter.

name: Voltaic Pile
description: Volta's pile: electricity tears compounds apart. Electrolysis unlocked.

name: Iodine
description: Courtois's iodine came out of seaweed: plants hide elements, and medicines too. The apothecaries send their herbs.

name: Platinum
description: Platinum makes reactions go without being used up. Catalysis unlocked.

name: Dry Ice
description: Thilorier's dry ice at -78 C. The race to liquefy every gas has begun: the Air Liquefier is unlocked.

name: Benzene
description: Charles Mansfield fractionates coal tar into pure benzene (1849): the Fractionating Column is unlocked.

name: Urea
description: Wohler's urea: organic chemistry is just chemistry. The apothecary's shelf opens.

name: Quinine
description: Quinine from cinchona bark: chemists race to extract every plant's secret.

name: Dynamo
description: Siemens' dynamo makes electricity by the ton: the Electrolytic Cell is unlocked, and oil, bauxite, copper ore and gold telluride are worth digging.

name: Sodium bicarbonate
description: Solvay's ammonia soda (1861) founds the heavy chemical industry.

name: Fluorine
description: Henri Moissan isolated fluorine (1886); his electric arc furnace (1892) reaches 3,500 C. The Arc Furnace is unlocked.

name: Gasoline
description: Gasoline for the motor car. Catalytic crackers will make more of it from heavy oil: the Catalytic Cracker is unlocked.

name: Stainless Steel
description: Alloy steel strong enough to hold 200 atmospheres: the High-Pressure Reactor is unlocked.

name: Aspirin
description: Bayer's aspirin (1899): the pharmaceutical industry is born.

name: Bakelite
description: The age of plastics. Natural gas and rutile arrive.

name: Vanillin
description: Tiemann and Haarmann's synthetic vanilla (1874): the flavour industry learns to make what plants make.

name: Welsbach Gas Mantle
description: Welsbach's thorium mantle (1891) turns a gas flame into brilliant white light: the rare earths find their first use.

name: Monosodium glutamate
description: Kikunae Ikeda tastes kombu broth and names a fifth taste, umami (1908).

name: Dry Cell
description: Gassner's dry cell (1886): electricity you can carry in your pocket.

name: Tungsten Carbide
description: Moissan's carbides: in the arc furnace almost anything will combine with carbon, and the results are nearly as hard as diamond.

name: Polyethylene
description: ICI's polythene (1933), found by accident at 1,400 atmospheres. Meanwhile biochemists hunt the vitamins in bran, egg and spinach.

name: Nylon 6,6
description: Carothers' nylon (1935): 'as strong as steel, as fine as a spider's web'. Stockings sold out in a day in 1940.

name: Sulfanilamide
description: The sulfa drugs work, and Florey and Chain need penicillin by the vat: the Bioreactor is unlocked.

name: Vitamin C
description: Szent-Gyorgyi and Reichstein's vitamin C (1933): the hunt for every vitamin is on.

name: Cemented Carbide
description: Cemented carbide anvils hold 50,000 atmospheres: the Diamond Press is unlocked.

name: Polysilicon
description: Silicon pure to one part in a billion. Teal's Crystal Puller grows it into one flawless crystal.

name: Transistor
description: The transistor (1947). The silicon age opens: the CVD Chamber is unlocked.

name: Uranium
description: Uranium metal for Fermi's pile (Chicago, 2 December 1942): the Nuclear Reactor is unlocked.

name: Neptunium
description: Neptunium, the first element beyond uranium. Lawrence's cyclotron will reach further: the Cyclotron is unlocked.

name: Streptomycin
description: Streptomycin cures tuberculosis (1944): the golden age of antibiotics, dug out of the soil.

name: MOSFET
description: Atalla and Kahng's MOSFET (1959). Every chip ever since is built from it.

name: Microprocessor
description: The microprocessor (Intel 4004, 1971): 2,300 transistors on a chip. Today's carry tens of billions.

name: Blue LED
description: The blue LED (Akasaki, Amano, Nakamura, 1993; Nobel 2014). White light from a diode at last.

name: Human Insulin
description: Human insulin from bacteria (1978): biology becomes a factory.

name: Oganesson
description: Oganesson (Dubna, 2002; named 2016): the seventh row of the periodic table is complete.

name: Sugarcane Juice
description: Steam sugar mills spin their syrup in perforated baskets to throw off the molasses, and Gustaf de Laval does the same to milk: the Centrifuge is unlocked.

name: Blood Plasma
description: Theodor Svedberg's ultracentrifuge (1924; Nobel Prize 1926) spins hard enough to weigh a protein molecule: the Ultracentrifuge is unlocked.

name: Sodium perborate
description: Henkel's Persil (1907): perborate and silicate, the first washing powder that bleached by itself.

name: Methylene diphenyl diisocyanate
description: Otto Bayer's polyurethanes (1937): two isocyanate groups meet a polyol, and foam rises in the mould.

name: 2,4-Dichlorophenoxyacetic acid
description: 2,4-D (1946), the first selective weedkiller: it kills the weeds and spares the wheat.

name: N-Vinylpyrrolidone
description: Walter Reppe's acetylene chemistry under pressure opens the vinyl monomers. Polyvinylpyrrolidone even stood in for blood plasma in the war.

name: Ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid
description: EDTA (Ferdinand Munz, 1935): a molecule that wraps around a metal ion and won't let go.

name: DEET
description: DEET (1946): the US Army's answer to jungle mosquitoes, still the standard insect repellent.

name: RDX
description: RDX, a medicine in 1898, became Britain's 'Research Department Explosive' in the Second World War.

name: Tetramethylsilane
description: Tetramethylsilane becomes the zero of the NMR scale (1958): chemists read molecules by their nuclei.

name: Ethyl cyanoacrylate
description: Harry Coover's cyanoacrylate (1951) was rejected for sticking to everything; in 1958 it went on sale as superglue.

name: Pentetic acid
description: Gadolinium held tight in DTPA (1988): the first MRI contrast agent lights up blood vessels and tumours.

name: Sucralose
description: Sucralose (1976): a student told to 'test' a chlorinated sugar thought he had been told to taste it.

name: Galaxolide
description: Perfume goes synthetic: Galaxolide (1965), Hedione (1962) and their kin are now the backbone of every fragrance, from fine perfume to washing powder.

name: Prontosil
description: Gerhard Domagk's red dye Prontosil (1932) cured streptococcal infections; the dye half turned out not to matter. The sulfa drugs were the first antibacterials.

name: Methyl tert-butyl ether
description: Unleaded petrol (1975 on) needs its octane from somewhere: the refinery ethers fill the gap.

name: beta-Farnesene
description: Synthetic biology: engineered yeast turns cane sugar into farnesene, a jet fuel and a rubber monomer.

name: Pyromellitic dianhydride
description: Kapton (DuPont, 1960s): polyimide film from pyromellitic dianhydride shrugs off 400 C and near absolute zero, and flew on Apollo.

name: 1,1,1,2-Tetrafluoroethane
description: The Montreal Protocol (1987) phases out the ozone-eating CFCs; HFC-134a cools the world's cars and fridges instead.

name: gamma-Undecalactone
description: Guerlain's Mitsouko (1919) wrapped a synthetic peach lactone in oakmoss; two years later Chanel No. 5 did the same with aldehydes. Perfume becomes chemistry.

name: 2-Hydroxyethyl methacrylate
description: Otto Wichterle's soft contact lens (1961): a gel of poly-HEMA that drinks water, cast on a machine he built from a children's construction set.

name: Bis(2,2,6,6-tetramethyl-4-piperidyl) sebacate
description: Plastics that survive the sun: hindered amines (1970s) catch the radicals that light makes, and are given back to catch more.

name: n-Butyllithium
description: Butyllithium starts the 'living' anionic polymerisations Michael Szwarc described in 1956: chains that grow until told to stop, and so the block copolymers of shoe soles and road asphalt.

name: Barium hexaferrite
description: Ceramic magnets: Philips' barium ferrite (1952) is cheap, never rusts and holds its field, so it went on every fridge door and into every loudspeaker.

name: Sodium periodate
description: Periodate cuts a carbon chain wherever two hydroxyls sit side by side (Malaprade, 1928): the cut pieces told chemists how sugars are built.

name: Imidazole
description: Imidazole is the ring of histidine, which passes protons back and forth in the active sites of enzymes; in industry it cures epoxies.

name: Ethephon
description: A ripening hormone in a bottle: ethephon gives plants ethylene on demand, and cotton fields open all at once for the picker.

name: Isostearic acid
description: A branch in the chain keeps a fatty acid liquid: isostearic acid is as stable as stearic acid without setting into wax.

name: Diuron
description: Diuron (DCMU) blocks photosystem II at one exact point, so plant scientists use it to switch photosynthesis off where they choose.

name: Fluorouracil
description: One fluorine atom where a hydrogen should be: cancer cells mistake fluorouracil for uracil and jam their own DNA synthesis (Heidelberger, 1957).

name: Tetrapropylammonium hydroxide
description: Mobil's ZSM-5 zeolite (1972) crystallises around tetrapropylammonium ions; the channels they leave later turned methanol into petrol in New Zealand.

name: Chlorothiazide
description: Merck's chlorothiazide (1958), the first thiazide diuretic: high blood pressure became a thing a daily pill could treat.

name: Pigment Violet 23
description: Carbazole dioxazine violet: so strong that a pinch tints a can of paint, and the base of nearly every purple you see.

name: Tartrazine
description: Tartrazine (1884): a coal-tar yellow that became the most familiar food colour in the world.

name: Ambroxide
description: Ambrox (Firmenich, 1950): the scent of ambergris, which sperm whales make, rebuilt from a herb.

name: A new era: Antiquity
description: Glass, soap, steel and spirits: the crafts of the ancient world.

name: A new era: Alchemy
description: The alchemists' acids dissolve almost anything, gold included.

name: A new era: Steam & Revolution
description: Coal, steam and the new elements: chemistry becomes a science.

name: A new era: Industry
description: Dynamos, furnaces and fertiliser: chemistry becomes an industry.

name: A new era: Modern
description: Plastics, antibiotics, the atom and the transistor.

name: A new era: Frontier
description: Chips, genes and materials built one atomic layer at a time.

name: Fully equipped
description: Unlock all 27 vessels.

name: The whole of chemistry
description: Discover all 2920 substances in the game.
